A small firm might need £20,000 to £50,000 for a refit, while a larger practice moving floors can need far more. Loanleaf handles enquiries from £5,000 to £2m and above. Fit-out costs per desk vary a great deal, so the total will depend on the standard of finish, and lenders will assess what you can afford to repay.

paying-a-tax-bill|professional-services.h1: Tax bill finance for professional services
paying-a-tax-bill|professional-services.title: Tax Bill Finance for Professional Services | Loanleaf
paying-a-tax-bill|professional-services.desc: How law, accountancy, consultancy and agency firms finance VAT, PAYE and corporation tax bills when fees are billed ahead of payment. Free introduction.
paying-a-tax-bill|professional-services.lead: Professional firms owe tax on fees they have billed, even while clients are still taking weeks to pay.
intro: A fee-earning business is mostly payroll. Salaries make up the bulk of costs, so PAYE and National Insurance are large and regular. VAT is usually charged when you invoice and paid with your return, which means a firm can owe HMRC for a £90,000 invoice that the client has not paid. Corporation tax then follows on profits, much of which is held in unpaid fees. Firms with a few large clients can feel this most, because a single late payer can delay a large share of the quarter’s fees.

Quarter-end billing often makes this worse. Firms invoice heavily at the end of a period, and the VAT on those invoices falls due about five weeks later, still before many clients pay. It is a timing gap more than a profit problem, and the question is whether to borrow short term, or to look at accounting for VAT on payment, which an accountant can advise on. Partners and directors sometimes ask whether the same finance can cover their personal tax, and it cannot, which is worth knowing before planning how much to borrow.
uses: VAT on unpaid fee invoices
Pay VAT due on invoices raised at quarter end that clients have not yet settled.
Payroll taxes in a fee-earner firm
Cover a large monthly PAYE bill in a month when billing has run ahead of collections.
Corporation tax on retained profit
Settle a bill on profit that sits mostly in work in progress and debtors rather than in the bank.
Partner or director departures
Fund tax due around a change in the team when a buy-out has taken the spare cash.
fit: VAT and tax loans for a defined bill

A VAT and tax loan is a short-term loan for a specific HMRC bill, repaid over a few months. For example, £55,000 of VAT might be spread over six months. Lenders look at accounts, VAT returns, debtor reports and bank statements.
Invoice finance for the real gap

Invoice finance releases much of an invoice soon after it is raised, which suits firms billing other businesses on terms. It can pay tax and wages while clients take their time. The lender will assess your clients and your billing.
Unsecured loans over a longer period
A general unsecured loan can be repaid over two or three years, with lower monthly repayments than a short tax loan. It costs more in total, but may suit a firm that wants to keep cash for hiring.
considerations: Personal tax is separate
Directors’ and LLP members’ personal tax, including tax on dividends or profit shares, is a personal liability. Business finance is not the route for it.
Look at VAT accounting
Cash accounting or other schemes may suit some firms and reduce the gap between invoice and payment. Your accountant can advise whether you are eligible.
Chase before you borrow
If a few clients are well past terms, collecting those invoices may solve the shortfall at no cost. A lender will ask about overdue debtors anyway.
faqs: Can a professional firm get a loan to pay VAT?

Yes. VAT and tax loans are designed for this. The lender pays HMRC or releases funds so you can, and you repay in instalments. Expect to provide VAT returns, accounts and bank statements. It will also help to have the HMRC demand and recent bank statements ready, so the lender can see the bill and how fees are arriving.
Is invoice finance suitable for a service firm?

It can be, particularly where you bill other businesses on terms. It releases cash against invoices, which helps with tax and payroll. Lenders will look closely at your clients and how you bill. Both are worth discussing, as each costs something and the better choice depends on how often the gap appears and how reliable your clients are.
Can I borrow to pay my own personal tax?

No. Personal tax of directors or members is a personal liability. Business finance is meant for company bills such as VAT, PAYE and corporation tax. Cover for a personal bill is a separate matter, and an accountant or a personal finance adviser is the right person to ask about it.
How do lenders assess professional firms?

They focus on fee income, recurring clients, debtor days and accounts, because there are few physical assets. A clear picture of billing and collections helps a broker place your case. A strong, recurring client base is often seen as helpful, though every lender weighs it alongside your accounts and existing borrowing.
Is HMRC Time to Pay an alternative?

It may be. HMRC can agree a payment plan, but charges interest on what is outstanding. A tax loan pays HMRC in full on time but has its own cost, so compare both before choosing. The route that suits you depends on timing, cost and how much HMRC will accept, so compare the total repayable under each before deciding.
